To install the Elevation Python package, use the command `pip install elevation`. Ensure that GDAL command line tools, including `gdal_translate`, `gdalbuildvrt`, `gdalinfo`, and `ogrinfo`, are installed and working. For installation details of GDAL command line tools, refer to the GDAL install documentation. Note that Elevation version 2.0 requires Python 3.11 or later. To check your system's readiness, run the command `eio selfcheck`.
To install the elevation Python package, use the command `pip install elevation`. Ensure that GDAL command line tools, including `gdal_translate`, `gdalbuildvrt`, `gdalinfo`, and `ogrinfo`, are installed and working. For Windows users, it is suggested to install the gdal suite at the system level to resolve installation issues. Elevation v2.0 requires Python 3.11 or later. For GDAL installation specifics, refer to the GDAL install documentation.
To install the elevation Python package, you can use pip to install the latest version, which officially supports Python 3. To install the latest version, run `pip install elevation`. For versions that support Python 2, use `pip install elevation==1.0.6`. The installation of GDAL command line tools varies across operating systems. For the lidar package, it is recommended to install from the conda-forge channel due to its GDAL dependency. To install lidar, run `mamba install -c conda-forge lidar`. For the latest version, use `mamba update -c conda-forge lidar`. For development, you can install directly from GitHub using `pip install git+https://github.com/opengeos/lidar`.
